news_headlines.title: Motorola Solutions to acquire D-Fend Solutions for $1.5 billion
news_headlines.summary: Motorola Solutions announced its definitive agreement to acquire D-Fend Solutions, a counter-drone technology company, for $1.5 billion. D-Fend Solutions specializes in non-kinetic RF cyber-takeover technology to neutralize unauthorized drones, and the acquisition aligns with Motorola's strategic expansion in the Communications Equipment industry. The transaction is expected to close in the fourth quarter of 2026, bolstering Motorola's offerings in public safety and enterprise sectors amidst expanding regulatory capabilities for law enforcement to mitigate drone threats.

Companies like LG Electronics and Samsung Electronics saw massive gains, and the Kospi index more than doubled this year, fueled by reports of Huang's upcoming visit to South Korea and a significant surge in the country's semiconductor exports. Analysts believe the South Korean market still has room to grow due to strong demand for memory chips and favorable valuations.

news_headlines.title: With DGX Station for Windows, Nvidia squeezes 1 trillion-parameter AI supercomputer into a deskside form factor
news_headlines.summary: Nvidia has announced the DGX Station for Windows, a deskside AI supercomputer capable of handling 1 trillion-parameter models. Developed in collaboration with Microsoft, this system brings data center-grade AI infrastructure to Windows ecosystems, allowing developers to build and deploy powerful AI agents locally. Powered by Nvidia’s GB300 Grace Blackwell Ultra Desktop Superchip, it offers 20 petaflops of FP4 performance and up to 748 GB of memory, aiming to remove the friction of moving early-stage AI workloads to Linux-based cloud data centers.

news_headlines.title: NVIDIA DGX Station for Windows Puts a Trillion-Parameter AI Supercomputer on Every Enterprise Desk
news_headlines.summary: NVIDIA has announced the DGX Station for Windows, a deskside AI supercomputer capable of running trillion-parameter AI models locally. This new system bridges the gap between powerful Linux-based data center AI systems and the Windows-centric enterprise environment, enabling developers, researchers, and engineers to build and deploy advanced AI agents directly within Windows applications and workflows. Powered by the NVIDIA GB300 Grace Blackwell Ultra Desktop Superchip, it offers high performance and secure agent development through NVIDIA OpenShell.
